subject: FintechCo integration - API auth & key management (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Huang <alice.huang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo integration - API auth & key management (post-call recap)

Hi Alice

Great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call on API auth / key management and the POC integration. TL;DR: Redwood supports API keys, OAuth/JWT service accounts, short-lived tokens, KMS integrations for rotation, and we can onboard a scoped service account for the POC.

Key discussion points:
- Auth flows: you preferred scoped service accounts + short-lived JWTs for backend-to-backend calls; we confirmed Redwood can accept JWT bearer tokens or standard API keys depending on your requirements.
- Key rotation: we support both vault-driven rotation (customer-managed) and Redwood-managed key rotation; recommended approach for POC: customer-managed service account + rotated API key for dev/testing.
- Scoping & least privilege: tokens can be scoped to per-route/model usage and restricted by IP/region.
- SDK setup: we provide SDK snippets for Node/Python/Go; SDKs handle token refresh if you use short-lived JWTs.
- Routing & fallback: we can pin requests to a dedicated endpoint or route based on region/latency; fallback policies available for model variants.
- Embeddings & rerankers: auth flows identical; access controls apply at the project/account level.

Action items / owners:
1) Marissa: share integration guide + sample code (attached) - today.
2) FintechCo: confirm preferred auth pattern (API key vs service account + JWT) and whether you need KMS/Vault integration - by Thu 6/30.
3) Dev (technical call): schedule architecture + security review (include Redwood security lead) - target next week.

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf, sample-code.zip

If helpful, I included a short example of a short-lived JWT exchange below (Node snippet):

// exchange-service-account.js
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
// create a JWT signed by your key (service account) and exchange at Redwood token endpoint
const payload = { iss: 'fintechco-service-account', sub: 'fintechco-backend', aud: 'https://api.redwood.ai/token', exp: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 300 };
const token = jwt.sign(payload, PRIVATE_KEY, { algorithm: 'RS256' });
// send token to Redwood token-exchange endpoint to receive short-lived access token

Happy to walk through any of these items on a short architecture call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Alice Huang <alice.huang@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: FintechCo integration - API auth & key management (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa - super helpful recap. A few follow-ups from our side before we schedule the architecture review:

1) Rotation & compliance: our security team prefers customer-managed rotation via HashiCorp Vault. Can Redwood integrate with Vault-backed secrets for both long-lived (dev) and short-lived tokens (prod)? Do you have an example flow?

2) Token scoping: can we scope a service-account-issued token to only access embeddings and reranker routes (no generation)? If so, how granular are the scoping policies?

3) Short-lived JWTs: we like the JWT exchange idea. What is the recommended expiry window for high-throughput embedding calls (to avoid excessive re-auth while keeping exposure low)?

4) Can you share any compliance artifacts (SOC 2 cert) or an overview of audit logs for key material usage?

Goal: agree auth pattern for POC so Dev can start the integration next week.

--
Alice Huang
Head of Platform
FintechCo
alice.huang@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Huang <alice.huang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo integration - API auth & key management (post-call recap)

Thanks Alice - great questions. Answers inline below, plus links and next steps.

1) Vault integration: yes - Redwood supports integrating with customer Vault or KMS to retrieve secrets for token issuance/rotation. For the POC we can show an example where Vault rotates a signing key and Redwood verifies JWTs signed by the rotated public key. See the attached short patterns doc (redwood-auth-patterns.md) and the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/redwood-auth-examples.

2) Token scoping: tokens can be scoped per-route and per-model. You can create a role that only allows access to the embeddings and reranker endpoints; policies are compatible with fine-grained route names and model IDs. Example policy name: fintechco-embeddings-only.

3) JWT expiry guidance: for high-throughput embedding workloads we recommend 5-15 minute access tokens with a refresh token or short-lived exchange token that you rotate every 12 hours from Vault. The goal is to balance refresh overhead with blast radius. If you have a high QPS that would make refreshs expensive, we can discuss a session-based approach where a persistent connection is authorized and refreshed less frequently.

4) Compliance artifacts: we can share SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and provide audit-log examples showing key usage events (issue/rotate/revocation). Neha (cc'd) is our security lead and will coordinate the documents.

Proposed next steps:
- FintechCo confirms Vault vs Redwood-managed rotation for the POC (you indicated Vault-preferred) - please confirm by Thu 6/30.
- Schedule 45m architecture + security review next week with Dev + Neha. Dev, can you propose 2 slots?

Attachment: redwood-auth-patterns.md (short patterns and examples)

Best,
Marissa
